literal.prompt: Как называется отдельная скальная вершина, окружённая льдом?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC glossary defines nunatak as a rocky crag or small mountain projecting from and surrounded by ice (L58-L60). Other choices are documented glacier features: crevasse (Science of Glaciers L120), icefall (L130), and ice stream (Ice Sheets L105). The set contains comparable glaciological features; only nunatak is exposed rock.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Cryosphere Glossary L58-L60; NSIDC Science of Glaciers L120,L130; NSIDC Ice Sheets L105.

literalGroups.literal: Это нунатак — скальный выступ или небольшая гора, выдающаяся из ледника либо ледникового щита. NASA отмечает такие объекты в Икесском хребте Западной Антарктиды.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC defines nunatak at L58-L60; NASA records these features in the Ickes Mountain Range at L278.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Cryosphere Glossary L58-L64: a nunatak is a rocky crag or small mountain projecting from and surrounded by glacier or ice sheet. NASA Landsat article L278: nunataks in the Ickes Mountain Range.

literalGroups.literal: При быстром течении ледника трение способствует образованию крупных трещин.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says crevasses are cracks in glacier ice and friction at rapidly flowing locations creates large cracks (L120).
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Science of Glaciers L120 (crevasse/crack; friction at rapid flow), L123-L124 (ogives below icefalls), L130 (icefalls at steep drops; faster, heavily crevassed ice).

literalGroups.literal: NASA отмечает нунатаки в районе хребта Икес в Западной Антарктиде.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA identifies nunataks in the Ickes Mountain Range at L278; the note adds a concrete Antarctic occurrence.
literalGroups.locator: NASA Landsat article L278: nunataks in the Ickes Mountain Range.

literalGroups.literal: Ледопады часто возникают на крутом перепаде; поток там ускоряется и становится сильно растресканным.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L130 says icefalls often form where glaciers flow over steep drops, where the ice flows faster and becomes heavily crevassed.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Science of Glaciers L120 (crevasse/crack; friction at rapid flow), L123-L124 (ogives below icefalls), L130 (icefalls at steep drops; faster, heavily crevassed ice).

literalGroups.literal: Ледниковые потоки — длинные полосы быстрого льда, ограниченные с обеих сторон более медленным льдом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC describes ice streams as long ribbons of fast-flowing ice bounded by slower-moving ice on either side (Ice Sheets L105), directly supporting this distractor note.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Ice Sheets L105: ice streams are long ribbons of fast-flowing ice bounded by slower-moving ice on either side.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Russian-speaking adults with thematic familiarity with glacier landforms.
absoluteDifficulty.ground: The technical term nunatak has no transparent Russian word-part clue. All four choices are named glacier features (crevasse, nunatak, icefall, ice stream); identifying which one is exposed rock requires glaciological vocabulary rather than broad adult knowledge. The definition makes it lower-end medium and avoids arbitrary calculation or length-based difficulty.
